affected.name: Cetus Protocol CLMM (math_u256::checked_shlw via get_delta_a)
affected.vulnerable_version_range: not published as a range; the post decompiles the live mainnet module at 0x714a63a0dba6da4f017b42d5d0fb78867f18bcde904868e51d951a5a6f5b7f57 (module math_u256) via revela.verichains.io

notes: Authors vanhoa and Thanh Nguyen, dated May 22, 2025, with an Updates note saying 'this vulnerability may affect other projects that use the same vulnerable math function'. Root cause as printed: checked_shlw is supposed to detect that a u256 overflows shifting left by 64 bits, but compares against 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF << 192 = 115792089237316195417293883273301227089434195242432897623355228563449095127040 instead of 1 << 192, so the correct test (value >= 1<<192) never fires; the 320-bit product then wraps back into 256 bits and the numerator collapses to a residue often just 1. The post names one attacked transaction and publishes no severity.

title: Cetus Protocol $260M Exploit: Root Cause Analysis and Technical Breakdown (Verichains, May 22, 2025)

notes: Attack steps as printed: the attacker set up and performed several swaps in tick range [300000, 300200], added liquidity paying 1 unit of token A but receiving a liquidity value of 10,365,647,984,364,446,732,462,244,378,333,008 (~2^113) because of undetected bitwise truncation, removed it immediately, repaid the flash swap and kept approximately 5.7 million SUI. Root cause as printed: checked_shlw computes mask = 0xffffffffffffffff << 192 with the comment 'This is incorrect!', so most values greater than 2^192 pass through undetected and the subsequent << 64 causes a silent overflow (Move shifts do not abort); the intended check was n >= 1 << 192. Tier 3.
